links.outcome: Reading grade level (FKGL) of ChatGPT patient-education answers versus average patient reading level
links.effect: Mean FKGL of all responses 11.65; original 12.15 and easier 11.14, above the sixth-to-ninth grade average American reading level and above most website FKGLs.
links.quote: The mean FKGL of ChatGPT’s answers, before and after asking for easier wording, was 12.15 and 11.14, respectively.

links.outcome: Reading level of ChatGPT patient materials relative to intended users' reading level
links.effect: Original responses FKGL 12.15 (95% CI 11.45 to 12.85); easier responses 11.14, still above the average American reading level of sixth to ninth grade.
links.quote: There was a statistically significant lower FKGL (t = 2.204; p = 0.029) for the easier responses (11.14; 95% CI 10.57 to 11.71) than the original question responses (12.15; 95% CI 11.45 to 12.85).

links.outcome: Consistency of ChatGPT accuracy, comprehensiveness, acceptability and FKGL when the same question was asked twice
links.effect: No significant difference between first and second asks: accuracy p=0.415, comprehensiveness p=0.171, acceptability p=0.176, FKGL p=0.793.
links.quote: There was no statistically significant difference in accuracy (t = 0.821; p = 0.415) between the first question responses (4.33; 95% CI 4.21 to 4.46) and the second question responses (4.25; 95% CI 4.11 to 4.40).

links.outcome: Reproducibility of output quality across repeated runs of the same question
links.effect: No significant differences between repeated asks in accuracy (p=0.415), comprehensiveness (p=0.171), acceptability (p=0.176), and FKGL (p=0.793).
links.quote: There was no statistically significant difference in FKGL (t = 0.264; p = 0.793) between the first question responses (12.25; 95% CI 11.29 to 13.20) and the second question responses (12.06; 95% CI 11.02 to 13.10).

links.outcome: Accuracy and acceptability of ChatGPT answers rated by resident physicians
links.effect: Mean accuracy 4.26 (95% CI 4.19 to 4.33); only 59.2% (71/120) of responses acceptable to at least four of five raters.
links.quote: Out of all the responses, ≥ four reviewers rated 59.2% (71.0/120, 95% CI 50.0% to 67.7%) as acceptable.

links.outcome: Incompleteness of ChatGPT patient answers judged unacceptable as sole information source
links.effect: Only 59.2% (71/120) of responses rated acceptable by at least four raters; easier responses had lower comprehensiveness (3.68 vs 3.91).
links.quote: This implies that ChatGPT may have been leaving out key elements of answers that a surgeon would include when responding to patients, and therefore may not be reliable as the sole source of information for patient questions.

unlisted_practices: Prompting the chatbot to simplify its explanation to lower reading grade level (reduced FKGL 12.15 to 11.14 but reduced comprehensiveness)
